instruction: Extract employee performance data from the Excel sheet and generate personalized PDF evaluation forms for each employee, completing the template with their details and ratings. Name each PDF after the employee and save it to the Desktop, using the checkmark symbol '√' to indicate their ratings.

metadata.explanation: This task requires creating individual PDF files for all 7 employees in the Excel sheet. Verified by reading the Excel file: there are exactly 7 employees (John Doe, Emily Johnson, Michael Brown, Linda Green, David Wilson, Sophia Carter, Alex Lee). The evaluator performs comprehensive verification: (1) counts 7 employee PDFs excluding template, (2) verifies correct naming, (3) checks content includes employee data, (4) verifies checkmark symbols present.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator checks all 4 key requirements from the instruction with partial credit scoring (25% each): (1) correct count of 7 employee PDFs excluding template, (2) correct naming matching employee names, (3) content verification that employee names appear in PDF text, (4) checkmark symbols present in PDFs.

Template contamination correctly handled: Getter filters out 'review_template.pdf' (getters/pdf.py:51-52) and metric uses 'employee_pdf_count' which excludes template. Expected count of 7 matches exactly the number of employee PDFs needed, not total PDFs on Desktop.

Metric parameter handling is correct: Line 29 uses 'expected.get('count', 7)' which correctly accesses the rules dict directly (when expected.type='rule', framework passes rules dict as expected parameter, not {'type': 'rule', 'rules': {...}}).

Logical correctness verified: Getter extracts PDF files and text content using pdftotext. Metric compares all aspects correctly with sensible partial credit logic. Data flow is sound: Desktop PDFs → filter template → extract content → verify count/naming/content/checkmarks.

Practical feasibility confirmed: Getter uses standard 'pdftotext' tool for text extraction. Edge cases handled (empty results, missing text). All verification steps are executable at runtime and can accurately determine task completion.
